item.title: 如何用英语谦虚地回应夸奖和感谢
item.description:
内容简介

适时地对他人表达谢意既是一种礼节，也是人与人之间关系的润滑剂。不止如此，如何得体地回应他人的感谢也是一门学问。在本期节目中，主持人步理和 Becca 就来聊一聊英语中有哪些回应他人夸奖和感谢的表达。怎么回应感谢显得更谦虚？怎么告诉别人 “别客气，应该的”？一起在本期节目中学习一下吧。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
Hi Becca, how are you?

Becca
I'm well thank you, Buli. Oh, I forgot to thank you last week for helping me with that video edit. I really appreciate you taking the time to show me how to do it properly.

Buli
Of course, Becca, no biggie! It was nothing. In fact, that leads us into this week's question. Let's have a listen.

Question
英语里有类似 “举手之劳” 的口语表达吗？别人对我道谢的时候我总想这么说，但不知道英语里怎么说合适，想请你们介绍几个。以及就是英语里有没有能夸别人 “出了很多力” 的口语表达呢？

Buli
大家好，欢迎收听 “你问我答” 节目。So, Becca, to go back to the video editing tips I was giving you, are you feeling more confident after I showed you how to do it?

Becca
A little. It's sometimes difficult to know which animation to use.

Buli
Ah, I can show you where I usually get mine.

Becca
That would be handy, thanks!

Buli
No worries, any time. And how about adding some sound effects?

Becca
Ooh, I'm still not sure exactly when to make the sound effects play.

Buli
OK, I can show you how I do that too.

Becca
Aw, you're a star, Buli!

Buli
Not at all, I'm happy to help. I can see that you're putting in some hard graft to get these edits right. Hats off to you!

Becca
Cheers, Buli.

Buli 
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我跟 Becca 正在回答一个跟 “如何回应他人感谢的话” 有关的问题。这位听众在问题中提到，当别人对她表示感谢的时候，不太清楚该如何用英语说出像是 “哎呀，举手之劳而已” 类似的回应。

OK, Becca, let's get into some of these expressions.

Becca
Yes! British people are sometimes thought of as being polite and apologetic, so we'll start with the expressions that make light of the action that's being thanked. For example, 'no biggie' is very common and it's the shortened version of 'no big deal'. You might also hear 'no problem' and 'not at all', and, if I say, 'it was nothing' or 'don't mention it', those also have the same meaning.

Buli
I see. So, sometimes when we respond to being thanked, we want to make it seem like it's alright because the action that took place didn't take that much effort.

Becca
Exactly!

Buli
在英国，人们其实很习惯于在受到他人的赞扬时小小地谦虚一下。比如，用 “no big deal” 或者它的缩略形式 “no biggie” 来表示 “没什么大不了的”。

Buli
类似的表达还有 “it was nothing（小事一桩）” 和 “don't mention it（不必挂齿）”。这些表达之间的共同之处，就是它们都有意淡化自己的所做的事，把它说成是一件特别小的事情，从而劝说他人 “太客气了，不用这么感激我”。

What about 'no worries', does that have a similar meaning?

Becca
Yes! Using 'no worries' is almost saying to the person that's thanking you that you don't require the thanks, perhaps because the action was small. We might also say 'don't worry', but it's less commonly used in the context of responding to thanks.

Buli
Right. 在受到他人感谢的时候，除了谦虚地表示 “自己只是做了一件小事”，我们还可以用 “no worries” 或者 “don't worry” 来告诉别人 “别放在心上”。

除此之外，我们其实也可以客气地表示 “自己很乐意帮忙，尽管找我就行”。Becca, what ways did we respond to thanks expressing this meaning?

Becca
Well, you did reply 'any time' when talking about helping me look for animations. 'Any time' has a very positive feel to it. It's like saying you're 'happy to help' whenever. Another response would be to say 'it's my pleasure'.

Buli
Yes, those do sound positive!

最后，这位听众还在问题中提到，想知道有没有能夸别人 “出了很多力” 的英语表达。Becca, I mentioned that you're putting in some hard graft to get the edits right. Can we use this expression to thank someone for 'putting in a lot of effort'?

Becca
Yes. 'Hard graft' is used in the UK informally to talk about hard work. You also said 'hats off to you' which is a very British expression that comes from the gesture of taking of one's hat to praise, congratulate, and show respect or admiration.

Buli
想要夸奖一个人 “出了很多力气” 的时候，除了说 “put in a lot of effort”，我们还可以说 “put in some hard graft”。在这个英式表达中，“hard graft” 的意思就是 “巨大的努力，艰苦的工作”。此外，想要夸奖别人 “干得漂亮”，我们也可以说 “hats off to you”，意思相当于 “佩服，佩服”。

Buli
Taking off one's hat feels incredibly British.

Becca
It does, doesn't it? And one last very British expression that I use very often to thank someone or praise someone is 'you're a star', and that you are, Buli!

Buli
Thank you, Becca!

Becca
Remember, if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Becca
Goodbye!

item.title: 如何区分 “sales（销售）” 和 “retail（零售业）”
item.description:
内容简介

“Sales assistant” 和 “salesperson” 有什么区别？商店里的售货员能说自己 “I work in sales” 吗？本期《你问我答》回答一位听众关于 “sales” 和 “retail” 这两种职业的疑问，并学习 “sales assistant”、“shop assistant”、“sales clerk” 等与销售和零售行业相关的职位名称及其用法。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
Hi Phil. You used to work in a shop around central London, didn't you?

Phil
I did! It was one of my first jobs.

Buli
So, if someone asked you what you did back then, would you say, 'I worked in sales'?

Phil
Hmm, no, probably not. I'd be more likely to say, 'I worked in retail'.

Buli
Interesting! Sales or retail? That's actually related to this week's question.

Phil
Let's hear it.

Question
我们说 “sales assistant”， “sales clerk”，这个和 “salesperson” 不一样对吧？那商店的售货员可以说自己 “I work in sales” 吗？还是只是指公司的销售？

Buli
欢迎收听 “你问我答” 节目。本期节目将要回答的听众来信提到了 “sales” 和 “retail” 这两个和 “卖东西” 有关的单词。不过，它们之间究竟有什么区别呢？

Phil
This is an interesting question, and not just because I used to work in a shop. It's partly related to how job titles don't always tell us what people actually do.

Buli
Can you answer that question though? Do they work in sales?

Phil
Well, maybe they do, or maybe there's a better word for it. If you work in a shop, you can say that you work in retail. And a retail business sells things to individual customers, rather than to other businesses. So, a shop is usually a retail business and so is an online store.

Buli
So, retail businesses sell to customers rather than other businesses.

如果你在商店工作，那么通常可以说 “I work in retail”，也就是说 “我从事零售工作”。这里的 “retail” 指的是 “零售、零售业”，也就是直接向个人消费者出售商品或者服务的商业行为和行业。我们平时在线下逛的实体店以及在网上逛的网店通常都属于 “retail businesses（零售企业，零售行业）”。

那么，“work in sales” 和 “work in retail” 有什么区别呢？

Phil
Well, this is where it gets a bit more complicated, or a bit more interesting if you're like us. There's a big overlap between retail and sales, but we don't always think of them in the same way.

When we say that someone works in sales, we usually mean that they are totally focused on making sure that their business sells more goods and services. They might only be paid commission, and they might have to meet targets every month.

Buli
So, they might actively try to generate 'sales'. 名词 “sale” 的复数形式 “sales” 有 “销售，销售行业” 的意思。如果我们说一个人 “works in sales”，意思通常是这个人的主要工作是促成销售、提高销售业绩。同时，“sales” 也有 “销售额” 的含义，比如，“generate sales” 的意思就是 “增加销量，促进销售”。

其它和 “sales（销售行业）” 有关的单词或表达还有 “commission（销售提成）”，也就是根据销售业绩获得相应的额外报酬。销售人员通常还需要 “meet targets（完成销售目标）”，比如达到公司规定的月销售额或销售量。同时，还可能还需要 “generate sales leads（寻找潜在客户）”，主动寻找可能购买产品或服务的人。

Phil
Someone with that kind of job could work in a shop, and their job title might be 'salesperson'. For example, phone shops or car showrooms often have very sales-focused staff. Other job titles that are common in the sales industry are 'sales executive', 'sales representative' (or 'sales rep' for short) and 'sales consultant'.

Buli
所以说，从事 “sales（销售）” 工作的人也可能在商店里工作。比如，手机店或者汽车展厅里的工作人员。在英国，常见的销售行业的职位名称包括 “sales executive（销售主管、销售专员）”、“sales representative（销售代表）”，以及 “sales consultant（销售顾问）”。

Phil
Many people with these job titles might not work in shops – they might travel to meet customers or sell to other businesses.

Buli
是的，并不是所有从事销售工作的人都在店里上班。有些销售人员可能需要外出拜访客户，也可能专门向企业或机构推销产品或服务。

你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在辨析两个和销售行业有关的单词 “sales” 和 “retail”，并学习相关的词汇和表达。

Phil
Now, getting back to a salesperson in a shop. A salesperson in a shop might be more focused on customer service, helping customers, as well as things like making sure the shelves are well-stocked. We might see these more as retail jobs, rather than sales jobs. And some common retail job titles are 'sales assistant', 'shop assistant' or 'sales clerk'. I used to be a shop assistant in a supermarket.

Buli
也就是说，如果一个人虽然在一家店里工作，但工作的内容主要是 “customer service（顾客服务）”，比如，帮助顾客解决售后问题以及确保货架上的商品充足，那么这类工作在英语中也会被称为 “retail jobs（零售行业的工作）”，而并不一定是狭义上的 “sales job（销售工作）”。

就比如，“sales assistant”、“shop assistant” 和 “sales clerk” 在中文里都可以被称为 “店员、售货员”，但它们在英语里，特别是在英国，通常属于 “retail jobs”。其中需要注意的是，“shop assistant” 在英式英语中更常见，而 “sales clerk” 则更常见于美式英语。

Phil
So, it's a bit complicated. A 'salesperson' might have a very sales-focused job, or they might have more of a general retail job. Or it could be both, the difference isn't always that clear.

Buli
让我们回到这位听众最开始的问题：商店里的售货员到底能不能说 “I work in sales” 呢？其实，这要取决于具体的工作内容。如果工作的重点是完成销售目标、开发客户或者想方设法提高销售额，那么说 “I work in sales（我在销售行业工作）” 就很自然。但如果工作内容主要是帮助顾客处理售后问题、理货等运营相关的店内工作，那么说 “I work in retail（我在零售业工作）” 往往更贴切。

至于 “salesperson”，其实这个说法本身并不能完全告诉我们这个人的具体工作内容。一个 “salesperson” 有可能是负责提高销售业绩的人，也有可能是承担更事务性工作的人。当然，也可能两者都有。

We hope that's answered your question.

Phil
Remember, if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Phil
Bye!

item.title: 辨析与产品 “溯源” 有关的三个单词：“trace”、“source” 和 “track”
item.description:
内容简介

一位听众想知道 “trace”、“source” 和 “track” 这三个词该如何使用。这三个单词都可以用于描述产品来源、供应链及物流运输等场景，但含义和用法各有侧重。“Trace” 强调追溯来源或过程，“source” 表示 “获取” 或 “采购”，“track” 则表示 “追踪” 或 “跟踪”。本期节目将通过具体例子，带你辨析这三个容易混淆的单词。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
Hi Georgie. How's it going?

Georgie
I'm pretty good, thanks Buli. I recently subscribed to a food delivery service, and it's really great! I get a box of fresh fruit and vegetables each week, and there are a few things I really like about it.

Buli
Oh yeah? Please share them!

Georgie
Well, I researched the business a bit, and I was able to trace their ingredients back to a few small farms. I like that they source their ingredients from small, family-run businesses. They also have an app which lets you track the delivery from start to finish.

Buli
Wow, Georgie. That does sound good. Perhaps you can share the details with me after this recording. You've just used some useful words – 'trace', 'track' and 'source', and that is what this week's question is about.

Georgie
Let's hear it.

Question
“Track”、“trace” 和 “source” 三个词在确定某物来源的时候可以互换使用吗？我想到的场景是农产品溯源。谢谢。

Buli
欢迎收听 “你问我答” 节目。这位听众在问题中提到了三个可以用来描述 “查明某样东西的来源” 这个行为的单词 “track”、“trace” 和 “source”，尤其是对 “农产品溯源” 来说。

So, Georgie, in this case, we're looking at these words as verbs. Where and how can we use them?

Georgie
Hmm, well let's think about my food delivery subscription. I said, from my research, I managed to trace the ingredients back to a few small farms. That means I identified the source of the ingredients. I discovered where they came from.

Buli
“Trace” 的意思就是 “追溯、探寻某物的来源”。比如，刚刚 Georgie 就用 “trace” 这个词来描述她 “通过调研，追溯了她订购的食品原料具体来自哪些农场” 的过程，也就是说，她成功找到了 “the source of the ingredients（原料的来源）”。在这里，单词 “source” 是一个名词，意思是 “来源，源头”。

But Georgie, you said that the food delivery company sources their ingredients from these farms. So, 'source' in this case means 'to get' or 'to obtain'. The meaning is quite different. So, let's hear another example to hear the difference again.

Georgie
Sure. I love the coffee in my local cafe, so I wanted to find out where they get their coffee beans from. I looked into it, and I traced the beans back to a supplier in Brazil. I found out where they came from. So, now I know that the cafe sources their beans from Brazil. They get their beans from Brazil.

Buli
And that's how we can use 'source' as a verb! 我们也可以把 “source” 当作动词来使用，意思是 “获取或采购某种原材料、物品或者信息”。就拿 Georgie 刚才举的例子来说，她喜欢的一家咖啡店会从巴西 “source（采购）” 他们使用的咖啡豆。

I think that all sounds pretty clear. Now, what about 'track'? You said the food delivery company has an app which allows you to track the delivery.

Georgie
Yes. 'Track' means you follow something as it moves or changes. Think about the app I was talking about. It lets me see when my fruit and vegetable delivery has arrived at their warehouse. Then I can watch as the delivery van drives to my city, and then around my neighbourhood, before it finally arrives at my house. I track the delivery.

Buli
也就是说，“track” 和 “trace” 的含义有所不同，表达的是 “追踪，沿着某条信息或线索持续地观察一样东西的位置或状态”。比如，在收发快递时，查看包裹所在的位置和状态的服务或功能就叫做 “track” 或者 “tracking”。

你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我和 Georgie 正在辨析三个和 “追溯，追踪” 有关的单词 “trace”、“source” 和 “track”。

从含义上来讲，如果我们想表达 “查明某样东西的来源”，特别是像这位听众在问题中提到的给农产品 “溯源” 这个说法，那么最合适的词可能是 “trace”，比如 “tracing the source of agricultural product”。“Trace” 指的是 “通过调查，弄清楚或发现某样东西的来源、事情发生的原因等等”。与之相比，“source” 指的是 “从某个地方获得或采购某样东西”；而 “track” 的意思则是 “持续地观察和追踪某样东西的移动过程或变化”。那么，Georgie，这三个词在实际使用中又有什么特点呢？

Georgie
This is a good question. When using 'trace', we often say 'trace something back to something', but it also works to say 'trace something to something', without 'back'.

Buli
在使用单词 “trace” 的时候，我们经常说 “trace something back to something”，意思就是 “追溯某物的来源到……”。不过，直接说 “trace something to something”，也是可以的。

Georgie，那么想用 “source” 来表达 “从……获取或采购某物” 是不是可以说 “source something from” 呢？

Georgie
That's it, yes. 'Track' is a bit different because we're talking about a beginning and end of a journey. You can use 'throughout' or 'from' and 'to'. For example, 'We tracked it throughout the supply chain', or 'We tracked it from its origin to when it arrived at the supermarket'.

Buli
是的，我们在使用单词 “track” 的时候，可以说 “track… throughout…” 或者 “track something from… to…”，来表示追踪一段行程从起点到终点的整个过程。

That's really helpful. Thank you, Georgie.

Georgie
Remember, if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你也可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Georgie
Bye!

item.title: 常见工作合同类型中的英语表达
item.description:
内容简介

你是否曾在浏览求职网站时看到过不同工作类型的英文表达，却不确定它们具体代表什么？“Full-time”、“part-time”、“permanent” 和 “temporary” 看似简单，却对应着不同的工作时间安排和合同类型。本期节目就来聊聊这些常见的职场词汇，帮你弄清它们各自的含义和用法，轻松看懂招聘信息。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Becca
I'll be honest, Buli, I've been a little stressed out because my contract is finishing in a few months and I don't know whether to stay here or work somewhere else!

Buli
Oh, Becca, I'm sorry you're feeling that way, and I hope you'll figure out what you want to do soon. But your worry is actually related to this week's question.

Becca
Really? Well, let's get into it then!

Question
您好，我最近想换一份工作。我在浏览招聘信息的时候注意到，一些用英语招聘的职位描述中会出现许多描述合同类型的单词和表达。比如 “full-time”、“part-time”、“permanent”、“temporary” 和 “contract” 等等。请问它们分别表示什么类型的工作？和中文里哪些说法对应呢？

Buli
欢迎收听 “你问我答” 节目。So, Becca, you're not sure if you'll extend your contract or look for a new job?

Becca
No. I'm also not sure if I want to continue doing full-time or maybe try part-time, so I have more time for things like travelling. And I don't know whether I should look for something temporary or permanent.

Buli
That makes sense. Something full-time would make you very busy, whereas part-time work would allow you some more free time.

Becca
Exactly. I'm really considering a part-time position.

Buli
And what about temporary jobs? Might they give you more free time to travel too?

Becca
Well, that depends on whether the contract has an agreed upon end date and whether I'll be required to stay in the UK as I work. Ideally, I'd like to work and travel at the same time. So, the flexible hours we have now are great, but I do have to be in the office sometimes. And also, if I'm travelling for a long time while working and going on lots of exciting excursions, I'm going to need to make sure that I'm constantly making money – and enough of it too!

Buli
Ah yes, a temporary job might end before you plan on returning home. It sounds like you're looking for a permanent job that allows you to work remotely.

Becca
Yes, that could be good for me. I wouldn't have to worry about being unemployed any time, and I'd be able to work from wherever I like!

Buli
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我和 Becca 正在讨论在英语环境中求职时可能遇到的各种描述工作模式和合同类型的单词和表达。

So, Becca, let's look at these different terms in a little more detail.

Becca
OK! We'll start with 'contract'. A contract is a general agreement, and when you apply for a job, you should absolutely take the time to read the contract! Also, in the UK, when a job is advertised as a 'contract position', it often means the job is for a specific period of time or for a certain project.

Buli
“Contract” 就是我们常说的 “合同”。如果想要具体指 “劳动合同” 或者 “就业合同”，我们可以说 “job contract” 或者 “employment contract”。不过，在求职的语境中，特别是在英国，如果招聘信息上注明了某个职位是 “contract position（合同制岗位）”，那么就说明这份工作不一定是长期的，而是 “专门为了某个项目或者某个短期目标而招聘的、有固定期限的临时岗位”。

You know, Becca, I carefully read my contract before I agreed to start working here, and I noticed that it also mentioned full-time and part-time work. Can you tell us more about that?

Becca
Yes! A full-time job is one where you work the standard number of hours for a company or organisation, usually around five days a week. Part-time means working fewer hours over fewer days.

Buli
“Part-time” 和 “full-time” 分别指 “兼职” 和 “全职” 两种工作模式。这两个表达既可以作形容词也可以作副词。比如，我们可以说 “I have a part-time job（我有一份兼职的工作）”，也可以说 “I want to work full-time（我想全职工作）”。

Working part-time might give someone more free time - they're working less.

Becca
Exactly. You might work three days a week, or just a few hours each day. A part-time job can still be permanent, which means the job has no fixed end date. Something permanent has the intention of lasting or continuing for a very long time, or even for forever, without changing.

Buli
没错。通常来说，兼职和全职与否并不代表一份工作是 “a permanent job（一份长期的工作）” 还是 “a temporary job（一份临时的工作）”。形容词 “permanent” 和 “temporary” 的意思分别是 “永久的，长期的” 和 “临时的，短期的”。人们通常会用这两个单词来区分 “不需要续签合同或合同时间相当长的长期工作” 和 “合同时间较短，只持续一小段时间的临时工作”。

Becca
For example, you might have a temporary contract for three months, six months, or a year. Sometimes a temporary position is created to cover someone's absence or to help with particularly busy periods, like seasonal work.

Buli
That's true. 有时候，公司或机构还会因为各种各样的原因设置临时岗位。比如，为了在某位员工 “absent（暂时不在岗）” 的时候找人顶替，或者是因为某段时间特别忙，需要额外的人手来帮忙。

And lastly, you mentioned flexible hours?

Becca
Yes. Flexible hours, or flextime, is a work schedule where employees choose when to start and finish their working day, so long as they complete their total required hours or tasks. And so, now I work flexible hours, but I'm still required to be in the UK because I have to be in the office sometimes.

Buli
“Flexible hours（弹性工作时间）”，或者 “flextime”，也是一种在英国和一些英语国家常见的工作模式。在这种模式下，员工可以比较自由地决定每天几点开始工作、几点下班，只要最后能完成要求的总工作时长或者工作任务就可以了。

除了时间，还有一种在地点上较为自由的工作模式叫做 “remote work（远程工作）”，意思就是员工可以自由选择自己的工作地点，通过各种线上手段完成工作。拥有这种工作模式的岗位就叫作 “remote job”。

And that's why I suggested a remote job. It's a job that allows you to work from anywhere in the world.

Becca
Yeah, I think a remote job would suit me well as I just really want to travel and see the world – it's my dream!

Buli
Ah Becca, I'm sure you'll figure something out to make your dreams come true.

Becca
Thanks, Buli! Remember if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

item.title: 辨析四个描述 “行程安排” 的单词：“itinerary”、“schedule”、“plan” 和 “timetable”
item.description:
内容简介

有位听众来信提问：在谈论旅行时，“plan、itinerary、schedule” 和 “timetable” 这几个词有什么区别。虽然它们都和 “安排、计划” 有关，含义也有一定重叠，但使用重点并不相同。“Plan” 是最宽泛的说法，可以指 “任何事情的计划”；“schedule” 侧重于时间上的安排和日程；“itinerary” 特指 “旅行录像或行程安排”；而 “timetable” 通常指 “公交车、火车等公共交通工具的时刻表”，也可以指 “学校的课程表”。听节目，一起来学习这几个与旅行相关的常用词语之间的区别。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Phil
Hey Buli, you look like you're planning something.

Buli
Well, I'm trying to work out a plan for next summer. I want to go on holiday, but I can't take much time off, so I'm going to be on a tight schedule.

Phil
Yeah, as it gets closer to winter, I'm gonna start thinking about what I can do next summer as well.

Buli
And we are not the only ones! Let's hear a question from one of our listeners.

Question
最近在办旅游签证，需要提交各种各样的文件。其中我发现 “itinerary” 和 “travel plan” 竟然不是一回事。请问跟别人说自己的 “旅游计划” 的时候，“itinerary”、“schedule”、“plan” 和 “timetable” 这四个单词有什么区别吗？

Buli
欢迎收听 “你问我答” 节目。本期节目要回答的听众问题提到了四个和 “旅行计划” 有关的单词。

OK, so we've got some related words. I think the biggest difference is probably how specific they are.

Phil
Maybe we can put them in action to give a better idea of how they are used. For example, Buli, you said that you are making a travel plan. Do you know where you want to go?

Buli
Well, I need to see which country I can get to easily. Then I can work out a proper itinerary.

Phil
Well, if you get the bus, it can be really cheap. Just make sure you check the timetable to see how long it takes. It can be quite slow.

Buli
Well, I did say that I was on a tight schedule, so I think I'll just look for a cheap flight, but thanks.

你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我和 Phil 正在辨析四个在旅行规划中常见的单词 “itinerary”、“schedule”、“plan” 和 “timetable”。

We just used a few of the words in our conversation. Now, let's go through them.

Phil
Yeah, so, some of this is about how specific words are, so let's look at 'plan', which isn't specific at all. You can have a plan for absolutely anything – including travel. We can use it in lots of different situations. It's just something where you say or think about what you want to do and how you want to do it.

Buli
是的。虽然 Phil 刚才提到，这四个单词之间的区别主要在于它们具体包含旅行计划中的哪些信息，但 “plan” 这个单词却一点也不具体。“Plan” 的意思是 “计划”。简单来说，不只是旅行，只要是针对某件事去想自己要做什么，以及大致上打算怎么去做，都可以叫做 “plan”。另外，“plan” 既可以作名词，也可以作动词。作动词时，它表示 “计划，打算”，也就是思考计划的过程。

Phil
Right, let's get more specific. A schedule /ˈskɛˌdʒul/ or schedule /ˈʃɛdʒuːl/ is all about time. It says what you're going to do and when you're going to do it. And it means we have expressions like 'a tight schedule' where you don't have any spare time or 'on schedule' which means by the time planned. Also, like 'plan', schedule is both a noun and a verb – if you schedule something, you plan when to do it.

Buli
没错，在描述行程安排时，单词 “schedule /ˈʃɛdʒuːl/” 或者 “schedule /ˈskɛˌdʒul/” 更强调每一步的具体时间，什么时候要做什么。我们可以用 “a tight schedule” 来表示 “安排得很紧凑的日程表”，也可以用 “on schedule” 来表示某件事 “按计划时间准时进行”。

Phil
In American English, a 'schedule' can be the document that tells you when buses or trains arrive, and it usually looks like a table. However, in British English, that's called a 'timetable', and a timetable is a table that tells you when things happen, usually public transport or lessons in a school or college.

Buli
So, we can say that 'schedule' and 'timetable' have quite similar meanings as nouns.

单词 “schedule” 和 “timetable” 都可以指 “用表格的方式列出公交车或火车等公共交通到达和出发时间的时刻表”。只不过 “timetable” 在英式英语中更常用，而美式英语则往往使用 “schedule”。

除了交通工具的 “时刻表”，“timetable” 还可以指 “其它写有比较严格的日程安排的表格”，比如工作安排的 “日程表” 或者学校里的 “课程表”。

Phil
So, I said this was about how specific words are. And a schedule is a kind of plan – but focused on times. Well, an itinerary is a kind of schedule but focused on places. Your itinerary is almost always a list of places that you will go during a trip. So, if you book a trip through a travel agent, then they will give you an itinerary showing you where you are going.

Buli
Yes. 跟侧重时间安排的 “schedule” 和 “timetable” 比起来，“itinerary（行程单）” 则侧重于路线和地点。它通常会列有你在一次旅行中要去的各个地方。比如，如果你通过 “travel agent（旅行社）” 预订一整套旅游行程，那么旅行社通常会给你提供一份 “itinerary”，上面会详细地列出旅游路线都会途径哪些城市、景点，甚至餐饮和住宿的地点。

不过，需要注意的是，有些人可能会习惯用 “plan” 或 “schedule” 来称呼 “itinerary”。虽然这样说也没有错，但我们依然需要注意这几个词各自强调的重点，以及在办理签证或者向旅行社索要行程单时具体需要旅行计划中的哪些信息。

Phil
So, as a recap – a plan can be anything, a schedule has times, an itinerary has places and a timetable is for buses, trains or classes.

Buli
希望本期节目能帮助大家区分 “itinerary”、“schedule”、“plan” 和 “timetable” 这四个可以表示 “旅行计划” 的单词。如果你也有类似的英语问题，也欢迎你来信和我们分享。

Phil
Remember, if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Phil
Bye!

item.title: 如何区分英语中的收据、发票和账单：“receipt”、“invoice” 和 “bill”
item.description:
内容简介

“Receipt”、“invoice” 和 “bill” 都是英语中常见的与付款、收费相关的单词。不过，你分得清它们之间的区别吗？哪一种是商家用来向顾客收款的，哪一种又是用来证明已经付款的凭证？听节目，跟主持人步理和 Georgie 一起辨析这三个单词的用法区别。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
Georgie, have you ever thought about the difference between 'receipt', 'invoice' and 'bill'?

Georgie
Hmm… I haven't, actually, but they're all related, aren't they? They're all about written forms of payment, but they are used in different ways.

Buli
Indeed. It's just that I always get confused when a company asks me to provide a 'proof of payment'. Well, in fact, a listener has asked us about this too. Shall we hear the question?

Georgie
Go for it.

Question
最近工作报销的时候发现英语里的 “账单” 和 “收据” 有好多种说法，比如 “receipt”、“invoice” 和 “bill”，请问它们有什么区别吗？比如，公司报销要求提供的 “发票” 和商家发来需要付款的 “单据”，英语里一般分别对应哪个词呢？

Buli
欢迎收听 “你问我答” 节目。本期节目将要回答的听众问题和我们在交钱或者收款时的三种单据 “receipt”、“invoice” 和 “bill” 有关。Georgie, we know that they are all paperwork involving money, but are they the exact same thing?

Georgie
Great question! Firstly, no, they can't be used interchangeably. The first distinction is that invoice and bill are used before a payment, and receipt is used after a payment. Let's talk about before payments first.

Buli
Right. A bill and an invoice both tell you how much money you owe, but a bill is more informal. You receive a bill in a restaurant after you've eaten, for example.

Georgie
Yes. So the customer will ask the waiter, 'Excuse me, can I get the bill?' and the waiter will say, 'Yes, here's the bill'. The bill tells you what you had and what it cost. You can then pay the bill, which means you make the payment via cash or card.

Buli
问题提到的这三个单词最主要的一项区别就是 “bill” 和 “invoice” 是提醒人们 “交钱” 的，而 “receipt” 则是 “已经付了钱的证明”。也正如 Georgie 刚才描述的，“bill” 在生活场景中更为常见，可以理解为 “账单”。我们去餐厅吃饭的饭钱、手机的话费、家里的水电费等等，都可以是 “bill”。在英语国家，人们甚至会用 “the bills” 来指代 “日常生活中林林总总花销的总和”，类似于 “必要的生活费，生活成本”。

Georgie
That's right. We earn money to pay the bills. Next is invoice. An invoice is a more formal document commonly sent by businesses to receive payment. It has information such as customer and seller details, the amount of money due and when it is due.

Buli
Freelance workers or contractors such as an electrician or a designer often send invoices after finishing a project.

和 “bill” 相比，“invoice” 的作用更加正式。“Invoice” 可以理解为 “账单” 或者 “商业发票”，和 “bill” 比起来，“invoice” 上通常会记载更多和交易有关的细节，比如交易双方的信息和交易的内容、时间、条件。当然，还有某一方需要支付多少钱。

如果你需要开具或收到了一张 “invoice”，那么通常可能是意味着你提供了某项比较专业的服务或者收到了某个公司发来的货物。Again, it is similar to a bill, but it's more commonly sent between businesses.

Georgie
Lastly, a receipt. This happens after the payment as proof of the payment. The word 'receipt' comes from the word 'receive'. It's given after the recipient has received the money. Going back to our restaurant example, after you have paid the bill, you'll often have the option of getting a receipt.

Buli
没错。单词 “receipt” 的意思是 “收据”，通常只有在收到 “bill（账单）” 或 “invoice（发票）” 并支付完成后，才会提供给付款人，作为支付完成的凭据。你或许已经注意到了，“receipt” 其实和单词 “receive（接收）” 同根同源，相关的单词还有表示 “收款人，收货人” 的 “recipient”。

你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我和 Georgie 辨析了三个跟 “交钱” 和 “收钱” 有关的单词 “receipt”、“invoice” 和 “bill”。

Georgie
So, to help with your confusion earlier, Buli: When paying at a restaurant, use the word 'bill'. When your company asks you for proof of payment, use 'receipt', and when a business sends you a document asking for payment, use 'invoice'.

Remember, if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Georgie
Bye!

item.title: 三个易混淆的单词：“tense”、“intense” 和 “intensive” 有什么区别？
item.description:
内容简介

在英语中，形容词 “tense”、“intense” 和 “intensive” 拼写相似，而且都可以用来描述某种紧张或高强度的状态。不过，这三个词的含义和使用场景有所不同：“tense” 可以形容人、气氛或局势处于紧张或焦虑的状态；“intense” 着重表达情感、体验或活动的强烈程度；而 “intensive” 则强调一项活动强度高、安排密集，需要投入大量时间或精力。听本期节目，跟主持人步理和 Becca 一起学习如何区分和正确使用这三个形容词。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
Hi Becca. It's been quite a busy week!

Becca
I know! I feel like I've barely had time to sit down.

Buli
You know what? Let's just take a break from all the paperwork, and answer one of our listeners' questions!

Becca
Count me in.

Question
您好，请问能不能解释一下 “tense”、“intense”、“intensive” 这三个单词的区别？这三个单词听上去很相似，但是我不确定他们的用法。比如，我可以用哪一个来形容像一天内去很多地方这样体力消耗大的活动？

Buli
So, Becca, how was your last weekend?

Becca
It was great thanks, but very intense! I went on a little solo trip to Ireland. I visited three cities in two days, so I was constantly travelling and sightseeing.

Buli
That sounds exhausting! But would you say that moving around so much was stressful or uncomfortable?

Becca
Not really. It wasn't a tense trip, it was just a lot! I managed to go to many parks and cafes, so it actually felt relaxed.

Buli
Oh nice! And, since you went to many parks, did you do a lot of walking, too?

Becca
I did. I tried to visit the parks in the morning when the temperature wasn't so hot. Walking in the heat can be intense.

Buli
I agree. Walking under the Sun can make you feel tired, can't it?

Becca
Yes. If I wanted to feel that exhausted, I'd have taken an intensive fitness course or something!

Buli
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在辨析三个看上去十分相似的形容词 “tense”、“intense” 和 “intensive” 在表达 “紧张的，强烈的，密集的” 这些概念时，分别可以搭配哪些事物。

So, Becca, let's start with the word 'tense', how is it different from the other two?

Becca
OK! 'Tense' describes a situation, or most often the feeling, where people feel nervous, worried or uncomfortable. For example, if you're waiting for an important phone call, you might be in a tense situation. You might feel tense. It's not an extreme feeling, but there definitely is some anxiety or worry there.

Buli
Yes. If you feel tense, you are probably anxious and don't feel relaxed. “Tense” 常常被用作 “relaxed” 的反义词，形容 “令人感到紧张、焦虑或者不自在的感觉或事物”。比如，如果你在等待一个重要的电话，一直没办法放松下来做些别的事情，那么就可以说你处于一种 “tense situation（紧张的、紧绷的状态）”。你还可以 “feel tense（感到紧张，感到焦虑）”。

和 “tense” 不同，单词 “intense” 描述的并不是 “紧张的心情”，而是 “事物、状态或感受的强度高或者程度十分激烈”。

Becca
Exactly. We can use 'intense' for things that are very strong, specifically demanding lots of energy. That's why I described walking when it's really hot as intense. You could have an intense workout, an intense discussion, or an intense day of travelling like mine.

Buli
Or, in our case, an intense day of work. 在英语中，我们会听到人们说 “intense workout（剧烈的锻炼、健身）”，“intense discussion（激烈的讨论）”。此外，我们还可以说 “intense heat（高温，酷热）” 或者 “intense interest（浓厚的兴趣）”。

Though we can say 'an intense workout'. But didn't you mention 'an intensive fitness course' as well, Becca?

Becca
I did. So, 'intensive' usually describes something that involves more time, effort or activity over a period of time. So, even though exercising can be intense, an intensive fitness course would push you to your physical limits over a longer period of time.

Buli
也就是说，“intensive” 和 “intense” 类似，都可以用来形容一件事的 “强度大”。不过，“intensive” 更加强调 “需要花费很长的时间和很多精力才能完成”。就比如，一次 “intense workout（剧烈的锻炼）” 很可能会很快就让你感到疲劳，但一节 “intensive fitness course（密集的、高强度的健身课程）” 却可能会用一整套锻炼量很大的课程内容充分挑战你的身体极限。

So another example could be that you take an intensive language course, where you study for several hours every day.

Becca
Exactly! Intense focuses on the experience. Intensive focuses more on something involving a lot of work or activity. You could say, for example, that the intensive language course, with focus on the language learning, was intense, 'Intense' focusing more on how the learning felt.

Buli
And if you failed that course, you could feel tense about your future.

Becca
Yes, 'tense' focuses on our feeling in general. I could say that Monday mornings make me tense, especially when we have an intensive training session with the whole team. Hearing all those different opinions can get quite intense.

Buli
确实。在描述一件事情或者一项活动时，单词 “intense” 可以着重表达对一件事的个人感受，形容一件事的 “强度高，让人感受强烈”，“intensive” 则更着重形容 “一项活动强度高、十分密集，需要集中投入资源或者花时间、下工夫”。而单词 “tense” 则表示 “人、气氛或者局势处于紧张或焦虑的状态”。

Well, let's hope next Monday morning isn't so intense.

Becca
I hope so! Remember if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Becca
Goodbye!

item.title: 英国人的宠物都叫什么？从宠物名字看英语文化
item.description:
内容简介

英语里常见的宠物名字 “pet names” 有哪些？事实可能会让你大吃一惊：原来在英国，许多人都会用人名来给自己的宠物取名，比如 “Luna（露娜）” 和 “Charlie（查理）”。除此之外，根据宠物的性格和外貌特征来取名也是十分常见的做法。宠物的名字里还藏着哪些与英语文化相关的小知识？听节目，跟主持人步理和 Phil 一起来了解一下吧。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
大家好，欢迎收听 BBC 英语教学的 “你问我答” 节目。你或你的朋友会养宠物吗？如果让你给你的宠物起名字，你会怎么起名呢？Well, in this programme, we are here to answer a question about pet names. Hi, Phil.

Phil
Hi, Buli. Yeah, we've got a question about how pets get their names. Let's listen to the question.

Question
我注意到不少人会给自己的宠物起 “fluffy” 之类的英语名字，好像这个词的意思就是 “毛茸茸的”，就像是在中文里管宠物叫 “毛毛” 一样。请问在英语里，人们会经常用形容词给自己的宠物取名吗？都会使用有哪些含义的单词呢？

Phil
It's an interesting question that I hadn't really thought about before. In fact, I didn't really know where to start until I found out that here in the UK, insurance companies have started publishing lists of the most popular pet names.

Buli
Wow, I've never heard of that. So, is 'Fluffy' a top pet name?

Phil
Well, while it's certainly possible to call a dog or a cat 'Fluffy', it's not actually one of the top pet names. Some of the top names, which seem to be similar for cats and dogs are: 'Luna', 'Bella', 'Charlie', 'Teddy', 'Milo', names like that.

Buli
Wow, they just sound like people's names to me.

Phil
Yes, maybe it helps people see their pets as part of their family. And one thing I did notice, is that a lot of the names are the more affectionate forms. So, I mean, I can picture a dog called 'Alfie', but I'm not sure about a dog called 'Alfred'.

Buli
Me too. 说实话，我还从没想到在宠物的名字里还能看出英语文化的一些潮流和知识！刚才 Phil 提到，根据某些宠物的 “insurance company（保险公司）” 公布的数据，在英国最常见的宠物名字其实是 “Luna”、“Bella”、“Charlie”、“Teddy” 这些人名。而实际上，英国和许多英语国家的人确实很习惯用人名来给宠物取名字。毕竟，这些宠物也常常算作人们的 “family members（家庭成员）”。

不过，用在宠物身上的名字往往都是常见人名的昵称或者缩写。比如，比起给宠物起名叫做 “Alfred（阿尔弗雷德）”，人们更用 “Alf（阿尔夫）” 或者 “Alfie（阿尔菲）” 来称呼它们。对于人来说，类似的昵称或者缩写通常是亲近的朋友或者熟人使用的称呼，显示了彼此之间的 “intimacy（亲近感）”。

Phil
Yes, so to make names more affectionate in English, you can either shorten them, or add 'y', 'ie', or 'o', to the end of them.

And, while human names are popular for pets, they're not the only options. As mentioned in the question, adjectives are often used, and these might relate to the colour. For example, a grey cat might be called 'Smokey' or a ginger dog might be called 'Rusty'.

Buli
Yes, these are often a bit more poetic than just simple colour adjectives. 除了人名，正像是这位听众在问题中提到的，人们也会用一些形容词来给自己的宠物命名。比如，一只灰猫就可以叫做 “Smokey”，而一只姜黄色的狗狗则可能会获得 “Rusty” 这个名字。

不过注意了，这种取名方式往往使用的并不是特别常用的形容词，而会选择那些有些 “诗意（poetic）” 或者有比喻或象征意义的单词。就拿刚才的名字来说吧，“smokey” 和 “rusty” 的意思分别是 “烟雾缭绕的” 和 “锈迹斑斑的”，是不是听上就去比 “grey（灰色的）” 和 “ginger（姜黄色的）” 要更神秘和形象一些呢？

Phil
Sometimes names are picked to show some aspects of the pet's personality. Dogs are often given names that symbolise strength. Names like 'Buster', 'King' or 'Duke' reflect that. And it might also be why cats sometimes get called 'Tiger' or 'Lion'.

Buli
也就是说，在英语里，人们还会利用宠物的性格特点或者自己对宠物形象的联想来起名字。比如，不少狗狗会被称作 “King” 或者 “Duke”，也就是 “国王” 和 “公爵”，以此来象征它们矫健的身姿和高傲的神态。而不少猫咪则会被命名为 “Tiger（老虎）” 或者 “Lion（狮子）”，听上去就挺夸张的！

你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在讨论英语中常见的 “pet names（宠物名）” 以及相关的文化现象。Phil, did you find anything else about pet names?

Phil
I did read that it might be easier for cats and dogs to recognise short, two-syllable names, so people sometimes chose those to make it easier to train their pet. And I also read that one of the reasons that we come up with sillier nicknames for our pets than we do for people that we know is that they can't complain about it!

Buli
So, a catchy name is not just catchy to us!

Phil
Seems like it. Though I think the most important thing that we've seen here is that while pets can have adjectives as names, it seems that more people use shortened, affectionate human names to show their love.

Buli
是的。简单来说，人们在英语中确实会用贴切的形容词来给宠物命名，比如 “fluffy”。不过，使用的通常会是那些有些诗意或者象征意义的单词。此外，大多数人很可能还是会用人名的爱称或者缩写来给宠物起名，特别是那些短小而且以 “y”、“ie” 或 “o” 等元音结尾的爱称。

Phil
We hope that we've answered your question. Remember, if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Phil
Bye!

item.title: 如何用英语沟通和处理工作中的失误
item.description:
内容简介

职场中难免会犯错，但犯错后应该如何得体地承认失误、表达歉意，并向同事或上司说明情况呢？本期节目中，我们分享一些实用的英语表达，帮助你在承认错误、解释原因和说明改进措施时表达得更加自然、专业。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
Hi Georgie. How are you doing?

Georgie
Hmm, I'm OK… a little bit embarrassed!

Buli
Oh no, why?

Georgie
Well, I was given an important project at work, and I completely forgot to finish it! I must've forgotten to put it on my to-do list – oops!

Buli
Oh dear. Well, you can make up for it by helping me to answer a listener's question. Funnily enough, it's all about work failures!

Question
Hi BBC Learning English. I have accidently failed some tasks at work lately, and don't know how to tell people about them. Could you share some expressions I can use to say 'sorry, I missed that' or 'sorry, I failed'? How do people mention their failures to other people in English, and/or soften the blow?

Buli
这位听众提到，自己最近在工作中遇到了点小麻烦，有一些事情没能顺利完成。在这种时候，怎么跟别人说 “我有些任务进展不顺利” 或者 “目标没完成” 可能还真的有些难以启齿。

Georgie
Gosh. Well, I can relate to this question! Don't worry. I can tell you exactly how I dealt with my situation.

Buli
Great! OK, so in your situation, it was your fault, so it's best to take accountability – that means you acknowledge your responsibility.

刚才 Georgie就提到，她最近不小心把一项工作给忘了。当我们由于自己的原因出现了失误的时候，经常需要 “take accountability”，也就是 “承担责任，主动承认和接受自己的错误，并采取行动进行弥补”。

What did you say when you forgot to complete the project on time, Georgie?

Georgie
Well, to introduce the issue, I said: "There's something I need to draw your attention to." Then, "I didn't meet the deadline, and I apologise for that." You could also say, 'I take responsibility for that,' or an informal expression, 'I dropped the ball on that.’

Buli
Those are some good tips, and they are all expressions showing sincerity.

常有人说 “真诚才是最大的武器”。在英语中，我们可以用 “There's something I need to draw your attention to（有件事得请你关注一下）” 来引出具体出问题的事情，然后再用 “I apologise for that” 或者 “I take responsibility for that” 来诚恳地承认错误。如果事情并不严重，或者你在和关系较好的人口头交流，那么还可以说 “I dropped the ball on that”，意思就是 “我不小心把那事搞砸了”。

But next, you've got to put forward a solution. You need to let your manager or colleague know that you want to reduce the negative consequences.

Georgie
Exactly. You could say, 'But don't worry, I have a plan to sort it out. Here's what we can do.' Then, you should tell them how you plan to fix it. In my case, I said that I would finish the project this afternoon, so it would only be a day late.

Buli
这位听众在问题中提到了一个很有意思的表达 “soften the blow”，它的意思就是 “减弱打击，降低坏消息的影响”。 而在英语职场中，“soften the blow” 的最好方式就是在呈现问题的同时提供一个解决方案。比如，Georgie 刚才提到的表达 “I have a plan to sort it out（我有个解决问题的办法）” 和 “Here's what we can do（我们可以这样做）” 都可以帮助我们强调自己已经想好了如何解决这个问题。

So, after owning up to your mistake, then providing a plan to fix it. What's next, Georgie?

Georgie
To reassure other people, the next stage is to show how it will not happen again. In my case, I just said: “I'll make sure to write a clear to-do list each morning so nothing can be forgotten.”

Buli
OK. But what about in a situation where an error has happened, such as the wrong email being sent out, or a spelling error in a report? What could you say?

Georgie
You could say, 'Let me get to the bottom of how that happened so that it doesn't happen again.' The expression 'get to the bottom of something' means you investigate the problem by analysing it deeply to understand why it happened.

Buli
That's very useful. I've also heard the phrase 'rest assured', for example 'Rest assured, it won't happen again.'

大多数时候，我们遇到的可能都是一些小问题。比如，偶尔忘了事或者写错了信息，并不需要特别复杂的解决方案。这时，我们就可以用 “Let me get to the bottom of how that happened.” 来表示 “我会仔细研究一下为什么出现了这个问题”，或者用 “Rest assured, it won't happen again.” 来向对方保证 “放心吧，下次我肯定不会再出错了”。

Georgie
Yeah, that's a good one. Very professional.

Buli
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我和 Georgie 正在讨论当我们在工作里犯错时，如何用英语承认错误、降低影响，从而维护好和他人的关系。

Georgie
I think the best thing to keep in mind is that you want to acknowledge the issue, apologise, give a brief explanation about why it happened, and then give the next steps. I made a mistake, and here's what I'm doing about it.

Buli
Yeah, it's all about reassurance. Something has gone wrong, but you're going to fix it, or at least learn from it.

Buli
其实不只是工作，我们在生活中有时难免也会犯点 “小迷糊”。比如，忘记和他人的约定、错过了见面的时间或者不小心摔坏了东西等等。在这些时候，直截了当地说 “Sorry that I missed that.（抱歉，我把那件事忘了；我没注意到那件事）” 或者 “I must apologise for something.（我得为一件事道个歉）”，永远比闭口不言给人留下的印象要好得多。

Georgie
Yeah. I dropped the ball, but I'll do better next time! Remember, if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Georgie
Bye!

item.title: 辨析四个与 “开始” 有关的短语：“kick off”、“get underway”、 “set in” 和 “break out”
item.description:
内容简介

单词 “start” 的意思是 “开始”。“Kick off”、“get underway”、“set in” 和 “break out” 这四个短语也都有 “开始” 的意思。不过，它们适用的场景却各不相同。比赛 “开始了” 应该用哪个短语来表达？一场争执 “爆发了” 又该用哪个？听节目，跟主持人步理和 Becca 一起学习这四个表示 “开始” 的短语及其区别。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Buli
Hi Becca, I can't believe how quickly summer went!

Becca
I know! Before we know it, schools and universities will be starting a new term again.

Buli
That's actually perfect because the question in this programme is all about different expressions meaning 'to start'.

大家好，欢迎收听 BBC 英语教学的 “你问我答” 节目。I'm Buli.

Becca
And I'm Becca. Today's question is all about the beginning of things.

Question
你好，我知道 “start” 和 “begin” 都有 “开始” 的意思，但请问 “kick off”、“get underway”、“set in” 和 “break out” 这四个代表 “开始” 的短语有什么区别？如果我想说 “新学期开始了” 用哪个短语最合适呢？

Buli
That's an interesting question. By the way, Becca, when does the new term kick off in the UK?

Becca
Well, in the UK, the new academic year starts in September.

Buli
Oh, it's the same in China. The academic year starts after the summer vacation, so it's usually in September that the new term gets underway.

Becca
Yes, then after a few months, the colder weather starts to set in, and students get to go home for the winter holidays. There's also usually an outbreak of colds and other flu-like illnesses. I remember always being sick when I went home for Christmas.

Buli
Hopefully, we'll avoid an outbreak of colds and flus this year!

Becca
Yes, Buli, let's hope so!

Buli
你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我和 Becca 正在辨析四个固定短语：“kick off”、“get underway”、“set in” 和 “break out”。

So, they can all be used to say 'something started', but what are the differences?

Becca
Well, let's kick off with 'kick off'! You first asked me when the new term kicks off in the UK. 'Kick off' is an informal expression meaning 'to begin'. It originally comes from football, where the game starts with a kick-off. Nowadays, we use it for all kinds of events. I could say, for example, 'tomorrow's meeting kicks off at nine'.

Buli
I see. So, 'kick-off' can also be a noun. “Kick” 的意思就是 “踢”，因此 “kick off” 原本描述的是足球运动中比赛开始时，一方球员首先把球 “踢出去，开球” 的动作。现在，我们可以用 “kick off” 来表示 “开始或启动一项活动，程序或事件”。并且，加上连字符的 “kick-off” 还可以作名词。

What about the phrase 'get underway'?

Becca
'Get underway' is slightly more formal than 'kick off', and it specifically means 'something has officially started and is now in progress'. So, for example, the academic year usually gets underway in September.

Buli
也就是说，“get underway” 这个短语和 “kick off” 比起来相对更加严肃正式一些。“Get underway” 的意思是 “开始，开始进行，开始实施”。人们通常会用这个短语来描述一项重要或正式的活动 “开始了，开启了”。就比如，一个新学期的开始或者一项重要工程的开工建设。

I think I've heard similar expressions in news reports and official announcements. A reporter might say 'a negotiation or a meeting is underway'.

Becca
Yep, that sounds about right!

Now, we also had 'set in' which we use for things that develop gradually and continue for some time, often without a clear beginning or time boundary. It's often used for weather, seasons, or feelings.

Buli
I see. So, I could say, 'relief sets in as we near the end of this hot summer'.

Becca
A great example, Buli! 

Buli
Thank you, Becca. 和 “get underway” 和 “kick off” 略有不同的是，“set in” 这个短语描述的是 “某个事物逐渐来临，一个事件或情况慢慢开始了”。因此，“set in” 通常搭配的是那些 “并没有一个特别明确的开端，渐渐形成或确立的事物”，比如天气、季节或人的心情等等。

And lastly, what about 'break out'?

Becca
'Break out' is used when something unpleasant or unexpected suddenly starts. We often use it with words like war, fire, violence, disease, or arguments.

Buli
Ah, that's why you used it with the flu.

Becca
Yes. And we can use the similar noun of this phrase 'break out' – 'outbreak'.

Buli
短语 “break out” 和以上三者最大的不同，就是它基本上只能用来描述某个负面的事物 “开始出现了，爆发了”。就比如，我们可以说 “an argument broke out in the meeting room（会议室里爆发了一场争论）” 或者 “a fire broke out in the basement（地下室起火了）”。人们也经常会用到相关的名词 “outbreak” 来指代某件事或事物的 “爆发，突然出现”。

Becca
So, to answer the last part of our listener's question: 'kick off', 'get underway', 'set in' and 'break out' can all mean 'to start', but if you want to describe the start of a new school term, it's best to use 'kick off' or 'get underway'.

Buli
是的。对于这位热心听众提出的问题来说，如果想要表达 “新学期开始了”，那么说 “a new school term got underway” 或者更加轻松和口语化的 “a new school term kicked off” 是在这四个短语中的最佳选择。

Becca
Remember if you have a question that you'd like us to answer, you can email us too at: questions.chinaelt@bbc.co.uk

Buli
你还可以通过微博向我们提问。我们的微博账号是 “BBC英语教学”。Bye!

Becca
Goodbye!

item.title: 谈论 “gardening（园艺）” 时常用的英语词汇和表达
item.description:
内容简介

在生活和工作空间里摆放绿植、鲜花，是不少人的日常习惯。在英国，很多人也热衷于在花园或阳台种植自己喜欢的花草，还会前往当地的 “gardening centre（园艺中心）” 挑选幼苗、种子和各类园艺用品。听节目，跟主持人步理和 Neil 学习与园艺和植物养护相关的英语单词和表达。

文字稿

（关于台词的备注: 请注意这不是广播节目的逐字稿件。本文稿可能没有体现录制、编辑过程中对节目做出的改变。）

Neil
Hey, Buli, do you know anything about the mud stains outside this studio?

Buli
Yeah… Those are probably from my boots. And watch out for your pants, too. Sorry I accidentally put a bag of compost on that chair.

Neil
What?!

Buli
大家好，欢迎收听 BBC 英语教学的 “你问我答” 节目。I'm Buli.

Neil
And I'm Neil. Since I've checked my chair and luckily, everything seems fine, let's hear the question.

Question
你好，我的英国笔友和我一样都喜欢摆弄花花草草，但有时候我不知道怎么给他形容我种东西的方法和过程，比如不同生长阶段的植物啊，花啊怎么说，还有松土和移栽用的小铲子和小耙子之类的工具和使用它们的动作。请问你们可以介绍一些这方面的词汇和表达吗？

Neil
I like this question because I've started to grow things in my garden, so it's good to share the vocabulary about it.

Buli
Yes. Any hobby has its own specialist set of language. Let's learn some of it in this programme.

Neil
Where have you been anyway, Buli? You've never worn boots to the office before.

Buli
Oh, I've just been to the garden centre. I've bought a pot and some seeds. I'm going to try to grow these flowers.

Neil
And you've got the other things you need? A trowel, watering can, a rake perhaps? I see you've got compost at least.

Buli
Yes, I've got all of that. I've even got a big garden fork at home.

Neil
Ah. Well, it definitely sounds like you like gardening!

Buli
Yeah, look at this picture of my garden. Everything is at different stages. There are some tiny seedlings here – you can just see the first green shoots. But if you look at those flowers, they've already got some buds. I just can't wait to see them bloom.

你正在收听的是 BBC 英语教学制作的 “你问我答” 节目。在本期节目中，我们正在学习和 “gardening（园艺）” 有关的英语表达。其实不只是在宽阔的花园里，哪怕是形容如何在阳台或桌面上养点花花草草，这些单词和表达也都能派上用场。

We've got quite a few gardening words here, so let's go through them.

Neil
Yes. For a start, some of them are related to different stages of growing a plant – 'seed', 'seedling', 'buds' and 'bloom'. A seed is the thing you put in the ground. You plant it. When you start to see the first tiny green stems or shoots above the ground, we can call them seedlings.

Buli
Then as the plants grow, you might start to see buds. These are the round shapes that flowers grow out of.

“Seed（种子）”、“seedling（幼苗）”、“bud（花蕾）” 和 “bloom（花朵）” 四个单词分别对应了植物生长周期中常见的四个阶段和形态。在英语中，“seed”、“bud” 和 “bloom” 这三个单词也可以作动词使用。

Buli
动词 “seed” 的意思是 “播种，种下种子”，而 “bud” 和 “bloom” 分别指的则是花草 “发芽，结出花骨朵” 和 “花朵绽放” 的过程。

We heard some of the tools that you can use to take care of plants as well – a 'trowel', 'rake' and 'fork'.

Neil
Yes, a trowel is a little shovel with a short handle that you can use to dig something small. A rake is like a hard broom with a long handle, but with hard metal teeth. We can use it to help prepare the soil for planting, breaking up big bits of earth. We can also use 'rake' as a verb to describe doing this.

Buli
The other thing we use for breaking up the earth and planting things is a fork – it looks a bit like the thing we use for eating, but it's much bigger!

在照顾花草时，我们也会用到许多特殊的工具。比如，“trowel” 指的就是 “可以单手使用的小铲子，松土用的小手铲”。而需要大面积松土或清扫土地时用到的 “耙子”则可以叫做 “rake”。要注意的是，“rake” 通常指的是那些齿部比较密集的 “耙子”，而只有少数分叉的 “草叉” 或 “园艺叉” 则被称为 “fork”，两者的用途是有些不同的。同时，“rake” 还可以作动词，描述 “用耙子松土、整平土地” 的动作。

顺带一提，和国内的 “花鸟鱼虫市场” 有些类似，在英国，人们也会去 “gardening centre（园艺中心，园艺卖场）” 来选购和园艺有关的种子、植物、工具和装饰品。

Then we had a couple of words to talk about where you grow things. We heard 'pot' and 'compost'.

Neil
So, compost is like soil, but it has nutrients that help plants grow. You can buy it at a garden centre, or you can make your own by keeping things like vegetable cuttings and fruit peel and letting it break down for a few months.

And unlike a cooking pot, a flowerpot is the container that you can grow things in. They are usually round and might have holes in the bottom to let out excessive water. Long and rectangular containers for plants are usually called 'planters'. 

Buli
是的。在英国，“长方形的园艺盆或花园盆” 通常被叫做 “planters”，“圆形的小花盆” 则可以被称为 “pot” 或 “flowerpot”。放在花盆里或者撒在地里帮助植物生长的 “营养土，堆肥” 在英语中被叫做 “compost”。同时，我们也可以用 “compost” 作动词来描述 “制作堆肥” 的过程。
